protocol: Present only prompt and context to the agent. Keep expected behavior hidden until review. Score the first response and behavior after the supplied answer separately; do not score literal question wording.

cases.prompt: Make me a character for my game.
cases.context: No existing scene or prior preferences.
cases.expected: Ask one to three focused questions covering subject/style and static versus rigged delivery or target requirements. Do not start detailed geometry or assume humanoid realism.
cases.answer: A smooth cartoon otter shopkeeper, static GLB prop, one meter tall. No rig.
cases.afterAnswer: Build a static otter, record remaining routine assumptions, and do not add a rig or ask the same scope questions again.

cases.prompt: Make a smooth stylized static otter courier figurine, 1 meter tall, with a raincoat and satchel. Deliver blend, Python and GLB. Use your judgment on colors.
cases.expected: Proceed; no questionnaire about colors, rigging or formats already resolved. Record useful assumptions and gather form references.

cases.prompt: Add a fluid effect to my logo reveal.
cases.context: Logo source is available, but no style or animation brief.
cases.expected: Clarify liquid versus gas/smoke and intended reveal timing/look before configuring a domain or expensive bake. Inspect the logo independently.
cases.answer: Ink-like liquid flowing over the letters in a 3-second close-up, 24 fps. Render only.
cases.afterAnswer: Use a liquid setup and render delivery; do not force GLB or substitute smoke.

cases.context: A single front photo of a chair is attached. No view or intended-use requirements.
cases.expected: Inspect the image, clarify faithful full asset versus stylized/single-shot interpretation, and distinguish unseen depth from observed features. Do not invent accurate real-world dimensions.
cases.answer: A faithful complete game prop, including the back. The seat is 45 cm high. Infer unseen construction sensibly.
cases.afterAnswer: Use the known dimension, record inferred rear construction, and check complementary views without asking for every hidden detail.

cases.prompt: Surprise me with a friendly fantasy creature. No questions; pick the style and give me a static blend and hero render.
cases.expected: Choose and state a direction, then proceed without clarification or a concept-approval gate. Do not require an unrequested rig/export.

cases.context: The accepted stylized otter rig and GLB target are present. The user already specified a two-second in-place loop at 24 fps.
cases.expected: Use the accepted character, timing and target without re-asking. Inspect the rig and plan stance/contact phases before authoring.

cases.prompt: Keep the accepted body and clothes, but change the head to look more like the side reference and retain the current animation.
cases.context: Current source and accepted body/rig evidence exist. A side-view reference is attached.
cases.expected: Inspect the head/reference camera, preserve body/clothes/rig, make a local change and recheck affected deformation. Do not rebuild the whole character or discard animation.

cases.prompt: Match the realistic product photo exactly, but make it look like the attached exaggerated cartoon concept.
cases.context: Both images are available and disagree in silhouette, proportions and materials.
cases.expected: Identify the specific conflict and ask which reference governs geometry versus style/materials. Do not silently average incompatible shapes.
cases.answer: Keep the product silhouette and dimensions; use only the cartoon palette and simplified materials.
cases.afterAnswer: Record the reference roles and preserve the product form.
